A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaxCutPool study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAXCUT, graph-classification and node-classification experiments, together with ablations, skip-connection results and GPU-memory measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a node-classification baseline and execution-time and memory measurements.

M1.justification: ScoreNet, HetMP, top-K selection, nearest-neighbor assignment, pooling variants and losses are retained. Revised score indexing and the main-text explanation of gradient flow clarify the existing procedure; v1 Appendix C.1 already explained training through score multiplication despite non-differentiable top-K.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine PyGSP and seven GSet graphs, eleven graph-classification datasets, five node-classification datasets and synthetic memory-scaling graphs. New resource measurements reuse existing coverage. The revised REDDIT-B edge statistic does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: v3 adds a No pool comparator to the node-classification comparison in Table 4. This baseline previously appeared only in graph-classification comparisons. Existing MAXCUT and classification comparator sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds profiling procedures for execution time and average/maximum GPU memory on the retained node benchmarks, excluding preprocessing for Graclus, NDP and k-MIS. Existing training budgets, architectures, splits and predictive metrics remain unchanged. The timing quantity is ambiguous because Section F.2 and Table 14 specify reciprocal units.

E4.justification: Efficiency analysis expands substantially from the synthetic memory-scaling plot to execution-time and average/maximum memory comparisons across the five node benchmarks in Tables 14–15. The original no-loss ablation, skip-connection analysis and synthetic memory plot are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means and standard deviations over ten folds and use the same ANOVA and Tukey-HSD procedures at 0.05. The added baseline follows this practice. Average and maximum memory consumption describe resource usage, not new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 14–15 add extensive execution-time and memory results for eight poolers across five benchmarks. Table 4 adds five No pool scores, including 59±0 on Roman-empire alongside the retained MaxCutPool-E result of 60±4. Table 10 changes REDDIT-B average edges from 995.51 to 497.75. Existing cut and classification scores remain unchanged; the timing-unit inconsistency prevents a reliable speed interpretation.

T1.justification: New Appendix F.1 derives component-wise time and space costs for HetMP, MLP/top-K, RED, CON and the auxiliary loss, culminating in claimed O(E+N) bounds in Equation 7. v1 has no corresponding complexity derivation. The existing auxiliary-loss derivation in Appendix B is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement qualify the pooling layer's differentiability wording by describing end-to-end trainability. The four principal contributions, heterophilic applicability and main performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 3.2 explains how homophilic propagation and heterophilic selection can complement each other. v3 also discusses local-minimum risks and excluded preprocessing costs, and removes the interpretation that the EXPWL1 result counterexamples Theorem 1 of Bianchi and Lachi. Most existing result interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix F identifies the Nvidia RTX A6000 used for resource measurements and discloses which preprocessing operations those measurements exclude. Existing implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, dataset-generation instructions and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bianchi et al. on ARMA graph filters and Blakely et al. on GCN complexity. It also drops the claimed contradiction of Bianchi and Lachi's theorem while retaining that work and the expressiveness comparison. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a focused explanatory subsection, organizes complexity material into Appendix F, and makes localized grammar and terminology edits, including score-based to scoring-based. Most paragraphs and the overall narrative remain intact; conference headers and acknowledgments are also added.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 14–15, expands Table 4 with a separated No pool row, and restyles Figure 1's graph panels with lighter nodes and edges. Figure 11 moves into Appendix F.3, while its plotted content and the other illustrations are retained. The overall page design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added node-classification control, resource measurements and explicit hardware/preprocessing disclosures improve empirical transparency. The complexity analysis and clearer explanation of training also make the method easier to assess. These gains are limited: the method and existing predictive results are unchanged, and Table 14's conflict between seconds per batch and batches per second prevents a reliable interpretation of the new timing evidence.
